text:
maria: quick check — are we comfortable shipping the query-surface versioning approach for dashboards? want to hand this to product next tuesday.
omar: +1 from infra side, but we need a clear fallback plan in the router for mismatched versions.
devon: can you clarify what "versioning approach" means here? is this on the route metadata or the payload?
maria: route metadata. idea is to add `route_version` and let console pin to v1/v2. will avoid client-side feature flags.
alisa: sounds good. main concern is RBAC mapping — v2 routes add finer-grained perms, we need a migration map for existing tokens.
omar: agree. i suggest a lazy migration: router reads token->perm set, if token lacks v2 perms, route to v1 handlers automatically and emit telemetry.
maria: ok — that's basically the RFC followup. devon, can you sketch the authz check change?
devon: short sketch:
```
// pseudo
let version = route.metadata.route_version || "v1";
if (!authz.hasPermission(token, version)) {
  telemetry.increment("authz.mismatch");
  route_to("v1");
}
```
we should rate-limit the fallback to avoid thundering.
alisa: +1. also recommend a migration endpoint admin can use to preview token resolution for v2. product asked for a self-serve preview.
maria: good call. add admin preview and a sampling flag to surface failures.
omar: one more thing — batching semantics differ between v1/v2 for long queries. router needs to preserve batching pools per-version to avoid head-of-line issues.
devon: yep — we'll keep separate executors keyed by `model+route_version`. cheap to do.
sre-bot: heads-up: rolling deploy of router-v2 scheduled 2025-09-07 03:00 UTC if changes land.
maria: thanks — i'll update the handoff doc with these followups (fallback telemetry, admin preview, per-version executors, batching quota). pinging @alisa for migration map next week. :thumbsup:
alisa: on it, will paste draft by monday.
omar: i'll add throttling and telemetry knobs to the router config.
maria: awesome, closing this thread — if anything blocks, reply here."
